## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 33 (*Aphāsukaraṇa*) is a Vinaya training rule governing the conduct of Buddhist nuns (*bhikkhunī*s) [SuttaCentral]. According to the rule, a nun who intentionally causes discomfort, annoyance, or vexation to another nun commits an offense requiring expiation (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. In the framing narrative of the text, the rule is prompted by an incident involving the nun Thullanandā [Hüsken 1997]. Because the rule is formulated in broad terms, subsequent Vinaya regulations serve as specific instances of this prohibition [Hüsken 1997]. In its exoneration clause (*anāpatti*), the only ground for exemption from an offense is if the perpetrator acts without the deliberate intention to cause trouble or discomfort to another [Hüsken 1997].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral include the corresponding Pātimokkha and Vibhaṅga rules across various Vinaya traditions: the Theravāda *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (pc 33) and *Parivāra*, the Dharmaguptaka (*Lzh Dg Bi Vb Pc 92* and prātimokṣa), the Sarvāstivāda, the Mahāsāṅghika-Lokottaravāda (including Sanskrit *san-lo-bi-vb-pc137*), and the Mūlasarvāstivāda lineages preserved in Chinese and Tibetan (*xct-mu-bi-vb-pc154*) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus independently identifies cross-language text reuse with the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-3), in agreement with SuttaCentral's Mūlasarvāstivāda identification [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali Vinaya, DharmaNexus records 400 shared textual segments across 99 texts, showing extensive formulaic overlap with other Vinaya rules, especially Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiyas 35, 45, 23, and 34 [DharmaNexus]. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
